Industrial production (IP) edged down 0.1 percent in July.

In December 2002 the Federal Reserve reclassified all its industrial output data from the SIC system to NAICS.

The major market groups posted mixed results in July.
The indexes for business equipment and for defense and space equipment both increased, while the indexes for construction supplies and for business supplies both decreased.
The index for energy materials decreased 0.4 percent.
In contrast, the indexes for primary metals, for machinery, and for motor vehicles and parts each declined 0.3 percent.
The production of nondurables decreased 0.4 percent, with output declining in all nondurables categories.

notes: Federal Reserve G.17 release of August 15, 2025 (19 pages as served, untagged, TeX/dvips output distilled by Ghostscript), cut to pages 1-15 with pypdf (see holdout3/SELECTION.md): page 1 masthead ('FEDERAL RESERVE statistical release' banner and seal, not checked: may be images or outlined type), 'G.17 (419)', the release time and date, the bold title, the first paragraph and the summary table with its note; page 2 the rest of the narrative with two underlined subheads and 'Release Dates for 2026'; page 3 the list of tables and a framed notice on the annual revision; pages 4-6 charts (not checked); pages 7-15 Tables 1-13 (page 15 ends Table 13; Table 14 starts page 16, which is not in the file). Headings: the bold title, the underlined 'Market Groups' and 'Industry Groups', the bold 'Release Dates for 2026', the bold 'Tables' above the list of tables and the bold box title on page 3; table titles ('Table 1' plus a small-capitals title) are captions. 'INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION AND CAPACITY UTILIZATION' is also part of the box title; the one-to-one heading match keeps them apart. Tables: four complete tables, chosen because their numbers can be checked or read with certainty. Header cells printed on two lines are written joined with a space ('2024 Q4', '2025 Feb.ʳ'); the superscript revision marks are written as the modifier letters ʳ and ᵖ attached to the word ('Q1ʳ', 'Julyᵖ'; NFKC makes them 'Q1r', 'Julyp'), and the footnote mark of '2024 gross value¹' as ¹. Table 10: 'Item' and '2024 gross value¹' span both header rows and are written in the top row; the three group headers span 3, 3 and 6 columns and are written in the first column they cover; the last header cell, printed 'July ’24 to July ’25' with apostrophes whose code point cannot be seen, is left empty (not scored). Negative values are written with ASCII hyphen-minus and without a leading zero, as printed ('-.2'; the minus code point cannot be seen; assumed, as in holdout2). Table 3's 'Memo' and Table 6's group labels are rows with empty value cells; Table 6's 2025 rows end after June (empty cells). Arithmetic checked while typing: Table 3 Autos + Trucks = Total and Light + Medium and heavy = Trucks (within 0.01), Autos + Light = Autos and light trucks (exact); Table 9 in the 2017 column (the base year of the chained dollars) Final products + Nonindustrial supplies = the top row, Consumer goods + Equipment = Final products, Durable + Nondurable = Consumer goods, Business + Defense and space = Business and defense, Construction + Business supplies = Nonindustrial supplies, Automotive + Other durable = Durable (within 0.1), and the same identities within 1 percent in the chained columns. Tables 6 and 10 were re-read digit by digit. must_contain: 28 phrases, each printed once (the table list on page 3 repeats some table titles, so titles are not used; the subtitle lines 'Millions of units, ...' and 'Billions of 2017 dollars ...' are used instead), none crossing a page break, none containing a dash, hyphen or apostrophe; 'Further detail is available on the Board' and the Table 3 note stop before the apostrophe of 'Board’s'. ordered: 8 anchors on pages 1, 2, 2, 3, 7, 8 (a Table 3 row label), 10 and 12. Noise: the only repeated lines are table notes ('r Revised. p Preliminary.', footnotes on the composition of manufacturing) that belong to each table, and page numbers; no running header or footer, so noise is empty. Absent: the framed notice on page 3 is justified with two one-word line-end hyphenations, 'an-/nual' and 'Ca-/pacity', listed in their split forms; the rest of the text has none. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 100-220 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
